hook: FIIs pour in ₹4,479 crore for a 17th session, while the US eyes 25% tariffs on Indian goods

mood.basis: proxy: 0.35 x S&P 500 + 0.15 x avg(Nikkei, Kospi)

stories.title: US proposes up to 25% tariffs on Indian goods under Section 301
stories.summary: The US has proposed country-specific tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods under Section 301. Among rice exporters, KRBL and LT Foods are on investors' watchlists. Shrimp exporters such as Avanti Feeds, Apex Frozen Foods and Waterbase could also see investor interest. Export-heavy sectors could feel the most pressure if the tariffs go ahead.
stories.why: Export-heavy sectors such as rice and shrimp face the most direct pressure if the tariffs go ahead.

stories.title: FIIs net inflow of ₹4,479 crore extends streak to 17 sessions
stories.summary: Foreign institutional investors put in a net ₹4,479 crore on Wednesday, stretching their streak of net inflows to 17 sessions. Indian equities and the rupee both rallied through the day. The RBI has also flagged a sharp revival in portfolio flows in November. Steady foreign money supports both the Nifty and the rupee, and traders now watch whether the streak can continue.
stories.why: Steady foreign inflows support both the Nifty and the rupee.

stories.title: Net FDI turns negative at USD 4.95 billion in September: RBI
stories.summary: India's net foreign direct investment turned negative at USD 4.95 billion in September, the RBI data showed. Gross inflows fell and foreign investors repatriated more money. Outward direct investment from India rose to USD 4.41 billion. Foreign portfolio investment dropped USD 6.652 billion in October before bouncing back. The weak FDI figure adds to questions on capital flows, even as portfolio money returns.
stories.why: Weak FDI adds to rupee and capital-flow questions even as portfolio money returns.

stories.title: Gold extends losses, falls below $3,500 as hot US inflation cements Fed hike bets
stories.summary: Spot gold slipped below the $3,500 level, a low not seen since September 2025. Hot US inflation has strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates, which hurts non-yielding assets like bullion. Silver and platinum saw slight gains. For India, weaker gold weighs on gold-loan lenders and jewellery-linked sentiment. Traders now watch US data for the next signal on rates.
stories.why: Weaker gold weighs on gold-loan lenders and jewellery-linked sentiment in India.

stories.title: S&P puts Nvidia on downgrade watch over board oversight weaknesses
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings has placed Nvidia on watch for a possible downgrade. It cited weaknesses in management and board oversight, following the brief resignation and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia is seen as the bellwether of the AI trade, and jitters around AI stocks have already deepened. A downgrade could spill over into Indian AI-linked stocks and IT services shares.
stories.why: Nvidia is the AI bellwether, so jitters can spill into Indian AI-linked and IT stocks.

stories.title: Schaeffler AG likely to sell 6% of Schaeffler India for ₹3,188 crore
stories.summary: Schaeffler AG is reportedly planning to sell a 6% stake in Schaeffler India through a block deal worth about ₹3,188 crore. The price is around ₹3,400 a share, a 5.6% discount to the previous close. The stock has kept falling despite strong September-quarter profit and revenue growth. A large discounted sale by the promoter can cap near-term gains in the share.
stories.why: A large discounted block sale by the promoter can cap near-term gains.

movers.name: Schaeffler India
movers.why: Promoter block sale of 6% at a 5.6% discount

stories.title: Carlyle cuts Piramal Pharma stake from 17.93% to 10.52% for over ₹2,211 crore
stories.summary: The Carlyle Group sold 7.4% of Piramal Pharma in an open market deal, about 9.86 crore shares at an average of ₹224.17 each, worth over ₹2,211 crore. Its stake fell from 17.93% to 10.52%. Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund was the biggest buyer with over 2.12 crore shares. The exit adds supply, though a mutual fund absorbed the largest slice.
stories.why: A big private-equity exit adds supply, though a mutual fund absorbed the largest slice.

movers.name: Piramal Pharma
movers.why: Carlyle sold 7.4% stake in an open market deal

stories.title: Diamond Power bags fresh ₹488 crore orders for Adani's Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC project
stories.summary: Diamond Power Infrastructure has received two orders worth ₹488.18 crore, including GST, from Adani Energy Solutions. They cover supply of 6,659.66 km of AL-59 conductors for the Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC project. Total orders from the project now stand at about ₹1,196 crore. Deliveries must be completed by December 31, 2027, which gives the company clear revenue visibility.
stories.why: A large order book gives the cable maker clear revenue visibility until December 2027.

movers.name: Diamond Power Infrastructure
movers.why: Orders worth ₹488.18 crore from Adani Energy Solutions

stories.title: LG Electronics India promoter to sell up to 2% at ₹1,709.30 floor price
stories.summary: LG Electronics Inc. plans to sell up to 2% of LG Electronics India through a block deal at a floor price of ₹1,709.30 a share. The sale would raise about ₹2,320.5 crore. It would cut the promoter's stake from 85% to 83% to meet minimum public shareholding rules. The move widens the free float, though the block sale adds near-term supply.
stories.why: Meeting the float rule widens the free float but the block sale adds near-term supply.

movers.name: LG Electronics India
movers.why: Promoter block sale of up to 2% at floor price

stories.title: Juniper Green Energy arm signs 150 MW NTPC deal worth ₹155 crore a year
stories.summary: Juniper Green Energy's wholly owned subsidiary has signed a 25-year power purchase agreement with NTPC. It will develop a 150 MW wind-solar hybrid project. The project is expected to bring in around ₹155 crore in annual revenue. Power supply is scheduled to begin on June 30, 2028. A 25-year contract with NTPC gives the developer a long and steady income stream.
stories.why: A long NTPC contract gives the project steady revenue.

stories.title: Deutsche Bank and PNB sign pact to fund corporate M&As
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank and Punjab National Bank have signed a preliminary agreement to finance corporate acquisitions in India. It follows recent reforms that allow domestic lenders to fund up to 75% of corporate deal values. State Bank of India has also entered a similar partnership with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group. The pacts aim to support Indian companies in their growth and strategy.
stories.why: Cheaper acquisition funding can support banks' lending and deal activity.

movers.name: Punjab National Bank
movers.why: Signed M&A financing pact with Deutsche Bank

stories.title: Medanta block deal: Dunearn sells 2.4% for ₹930 crore
stories.summary: Dunearn Investments sold a 2.4% stake in Medanta for ₹930.01 crore through a block deal on the NSE. The buyers included HDFC Mutual Fund and SBI Mutual Fund. A block deal is a large single trade between big investors. Domestic funds taking the shares shows demand for the stock even as an early investor sells down.
stories.why: Mutual fund buying shows domestic demand for the stock.

stories.title: Asian markets rise as Wall Street rebound lifts sentiment
stories.summary: Asian markets rose after a sharp recovery in US stocks. MSCI's Asia Pacific index gained 0.4%, while South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 1.88% and 1.85%. Worries over AI spending, sticky inflation, higher US tariffs and interest rates remain in focus. A firm Asian tone usually helps Indian markets open on a positive note.
stories.why: A firm Asian tone supports an upbeat open in India.

stories.title: Bank of Korea resumes tightening with quarter-point hike to 3.25%
stories.summary: The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25%. It follows a pause in October and continues the tightening cycle. Growth forecasts were upgraded to 3.9% for this year and 4.1% for next year. Policymakers stay cautious because inflation is elevated and the housing market is heated. Another central bank hiking adds to the global rate-hike mood.
stories.why: Another central bank hiking adds to the global rate-hike mood.

stories.title: US proposes tariffs on 14 trading partners, adds 20% on China
stories.summary: The US on Wednesday proposed country-specific tariffs on goods from 14 major trading partners, including India, Japan and the European Union. It also plans an additional 20% tariff on imports from China. The news added to pain in US technology shares and to investor worries about volatility. Indian exporters are watching how the final rates are set.
stories.why: New tariff risk keeps global investors cautious.

stories.title: Nifty surges nearly 600 points towards 25,900; HUL jumps 5%
stories.summary: Buying stayed strong in the second half of Wednesday's session. The Nifty surged nearly 600 points to approach the 25,900 mark. The Nifty Bank rallied around 1,400 points and reclaimed the 64,000 level. HDFC Life, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank were among the top gainers, and Hindustan Unilever jumped 5%. Banks and FMCG led the broad rally.
stories.why: Broad buying in banks and FMCG lifted the benchmark indices.

stories.title: Nifty FMCG set for best month in 17 years
stories.summary: The Nifty FMCG index is poised for its best monthly advance in 17 years. Most of its constituents have gained between 10% and 20% so far this month. As a result, apart from Varun Beverages, none of the stocks have an upside potential of more than 10% from current levels. The sharp run-up leaves less room for further gains.
stories.why: A strong month leaves little upside in most FMCG names.

stories.title: Suzlon to invest ₹200 crore in Tamil Nadu blade plant
stories.summary: Suzlon Energy will invest ₹200 crore in a new plant in Tamil Nadu. It will add 1 GW of blade manufacturing capacity. The plant will make advanced wind turbine blades of up to 95 metres in length. These are for the S175 5 MW turbine, which the company calls India's tallest and most powerful. The extra capacity helps Suzlon take on larger turbine orders.
stories.why: More blade capacity lets Suzlon serve larger turbine orders.

movers.name: Suzlon Energy
movers.why: ₹200 crore plant adds 1 GW blade capacity

stories.title: PhonePe resumes IPO process, targets $12-15 billion valuation
stories.summary: PhonePe has resumed its initial public offering after deferring it on market uncertainty. It targets a listing at a valuation of $12-15 billion in February-March. It expects to raise about ₹12,000-14,000 crore through an offer-for-sale, where existing holders sell shares. The digital payments firm has reported strong revenue growth and is profitable at the group level.
stories.why: A large fintech listing could revive India's IPO pipeline.

stories.title: Sebi mulls early payout of up to 80% of sale proceeds to FPOs
stories.summary: Sebi has proposed an early payout framework for Farmer Producer Organisations trading in commodity derivatives. It would let them receive up to 80% of sale proceeds before the contract expires. The aim is to ease liquidity problems and give farmers timely payments. Corporate trading members would offer the facility, subject to certain conditions and net worth requirements.
stories.why: Quicker payments could ease cash shortages for farmers.

stories.title: Dollar steady as sliding yields temper safe-haven bid
stories.summary: The US dollar steadied after dipping to a one-week low, helped by a drop in Treasury yields. Upcoming economic data hints at possible interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve in December. The yen edged up against the dollar, while the euro held steady as traders waited for accounts of the ECB meeting. A steadier dollar helps emerging-market currencies.
stories.why: A steadier dollar helps emerging-market currencies such as the rupee.

stories.title: JPMorgan sees $450 billion AI debt blitz in 2027 before plateau
stories.summary: JPMorgan analysts expect companies to raise $450 billion in public high-grade debt markets next year to finance AI-related capital spending. They also see a growth plateau for the industry further down the road. The forecast shows how much money is flowing into AI infrastructure, and it keeps the AI spending theme in focus for global investors.
stories.why: Heavy AI borrowing keeps the AI-capex theme in focus.

stories.title: Sebi closes proceedings against Lloyds Enterprises after settlement
stories.summary: Sebi has closed adjudication proceedings against Lloyds Enterprises and two senior executives after a settlement. The case involved alleged irregularities in ₹144.82 crore of interest-free advances, failure to disclose related-party transactions and lapses in accounting for possible losses. Closing the case removes a regulatory overhang from the company, which can ease concerns for investors who follow the stock.
stories.why: Closing the case removes a regulatory overhang for the company.

stories.title: UBS keeps ₹1.50 lakh target for gold despite 27% fall from January peak
stories.summary: UBS has kept its Attractive rating on gold and forecasts $5,000 an ounce by December 2027, despite a 27% decline from the January peak. The bank cites central-bank buying, rising sovereign debt, geopolitical uncertainty and Chinese demand as long-term supports. The call stands in contrast to gold's recent sharp fall, which has hit sentiment among Indian buyers.
stories.why: A bullish long-term call contrasts with gold's sharp recent drop.

stories.title: Apeejay Park Hotels signs 42-room resort near Puducherry
stories.summary: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels has signed a 42-room resort under its Zone Connect by The Park brand near Auroville, on the Tamil Nadu-Puducherry border. It is expected to open in Q1 FY28. The property will have guest rooms, cottages, private pool villas, dining facilities and banquet venues with a combined capacity of 500 guests, adding to the chain's footprint.
stories.why: Asset-light signings let hotel chains grow without heavy spending.

stories.title: Bitcoin miners hammered again as price rout squeezes margins
stories.summary: The plunge in bitcoin is putting pressure on billion-dollar mining companies. They are being pushed to sell their remaining token reserves, both to cover steep operating costs and to fund an increasingly strained pivot into AI data centres. The crypto rout squeezes margins and adds to the cautious mood in technology stocks, as investors weigh how long the price slide may last.
stories.why: The crypto slide adds to risk-off mood in tech.
